I farm 7 mu, so I will not spread myself too thin. I will keep the main money on the wheat-maize land, because that is what I know best and what people around me do. I will put 5 mu into winter wheat and then summer maize on that same 5 mu, and I will keep 2 mu for peanut. I do not like taking chances at the start of the year. If last year’s seed and fertilizer level gave me a steady harvest, I will stay close to that and only push a little where I think yield can still come. Wheat needs the most careful feeding on my land, so I will give it a full base fertilizer and then chase it once when it turns green. Maize I will also feed enough, because if maize is short of fertilizer after wheat, the ears stay small and I lose money. Peanut I will not push too much nitrogen, because too much vine is no good; I will use more phosphorus and potassium there. Since I have well irrigation, I will not let the wheat suffer for water, and I will give maize water at the key time if rain is short. I watch what the better fields nearby do, and I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than watch yield fall.
